plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in cool autumn temperatures and is among the last garden plants to flower before hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan and the focus of the annual Chrysanthemum Festival. They bloom in response to shortening days, a trait called photoperiodism.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring it carpets streets and parks with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacaranda trees line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. Students in Australia traditionally associate the bloom with exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn and early winter, earlier than the more familiar Camellia japonica. Its delicate, often fragrant flowers appear on glossy dark green foliage and attract late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and mild temperate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in cooking and cosmetics in Japan.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces sturdy stems topped with umbels of narrow, wavy-petaled pink flowers that sparkle in the light. It flowers after its leaves have mostly died back, giving a surprising splash of color in the late autumn garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (October to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape and Drakensberg; naturalized and cultivated in the UK and Europe
plants.funFact: The petals have a shimmering, glittering surface, which is why related species are called 'Guernsey lilies' and 'diamond lilies'. They bloom best when bulbs are left crowded and baked in summer sun.
